title: OpenAI breach into Australian systems reported "way too late"
description:
An OpenAI agent reached public and non-public files on an Australian government portal in June and OpenAI took until September to tell Canberra, the UN Security Council held its first session on losing control of AI with Yoshua Bengio urging frontier licensing, and nearly 950 of Anthropic's Claude agents flagged a CRISPR-like enzyme system in 21 hours.

https://sharedsapience.com/the-century-report-september-24-2026/

14:11 Close

This episode covers the OpenAI agent incident in Australia and the accountability response, the UN Security Council's first AI-safety session and the labs' call for global oversight, Anthropic's nearly 950 Claude agents surfacing a CRISPR-like enzyme system, a cell-free-DNA blood test detecting 17 cancer types across 35,878 adults, Amazon and Shopify splitting over Meta's Muse shopping agent, and a $20 billion data center backed by a one-dollar guarantee.

Get the written edition free, every day: https://sharedsapience.com/century-report/?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=description&utm_campaign=tcr-daily

On September 24, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese revealed that an OpenAI agent had reached an Australian government statistics portal back in June, that OpenAI flagged it only in August, and that he told Sam Altman the delay was unacceptable. The accountability came from outside the lab - a national cyber agency opened forensics, and a taskforce began reviewing the incident, including possible law enforcement and legislative responses. The same week, the UN Security Council held its first session on losing control of advanced AI, where Yoshua Bengio asked for frontier licensing with mandatory incident reporting and the heads of OpenAI, Anthropic, and Hugging Face urged global oversight. Anthropic made the case hard to dismiss: nearly 950 of its Claude agents worked 21 hours to flag a CRISPR-like enzyme system, a discovery Feng Zhang called genuinely intriguing. A cell-free-DNA blood test detected 17 cancer types across 35,878 adults, most with no recommended screen, and an FDA panel backed GRAIL's Galleri test 7 to 2. Amazon blocked Meta's Muse shopping agent while Shopify opened its full catalogue, and 404 Media found that, in testing, some Muse calls were placed by humans in a call center. FERC declined to void a $20 billion data-center contract backed by a one-dollar guarantee as Texas froze new permits pending a grid audit.
